Hero.Title: Artificial intelligence consulting
Hero.Description: Independent AI consulting, from discovery workshop to production. Together we choose the use cases worth pursuing and the right model, including open-source models hosted in Switzerland.

Presentation.Intro: Most AI projects do not fail because of the model, but because the use case was poorly chosen or nobody had set the rules. Our work therefore starts with your processes: where time goes, which decisions repeat, what data is involved. The choice of model comes afterwards, and it is not tied to any vendor.

Why.Title: Why independent consulting
Why.Text: An OpenAI model on Azure, a model from Anthropic or Mistral, or an open-source model such as Llama, Qwen or Gemma each have different strengths, different costs and different consequences for your data. An integrator tied to a single vendor will offer you its platform. We compare the options on your case, with your documents, and we also tell you when AI is not the right answer.

Automation.Title: Sorting files and requests
Automation.Text: A model reads each incoming file and sorts it according to your rules: those that can follow a simple route and those, fewer in number, that need a human eye. Low-value claims, supplier invoices, customer requests, compliance alerts: the principle is the same, and the rules are yours.

Analytics.Title: Document extraction and checking
Analytics.Text: Invoices, contracts, forms, identity documents, reports: the model extracts the useful information, checks that a file is complete and flags inconsistencies. Your teams review the discrepancies instead of re-entering everything.

Chatbots.Title: Internal assistants on your documents
Chatbots.Text: An assistant that answers from your procedures, contracts and files, citing its sources. It can run in Microsoft 365, in your business tools or on infrastructure hosted in Switzerland, depending on how sensitive the content is.

Custom.Title: Integration into your tools
Custom.Text: Useful AI lives where your teams work: email, ERP, business software, document management. We handle the integration, access rights, logging and monitoring, and we document everything for your IT team.

Approach.Title: Our method, from workshop to production
Approach.Text: Six steps, each with a deliverable and a clear decision: continue, adjust or stop.

Steps.Title: Discovery workshop
Steps.Text: A working session with your business and IT teams. We review your processes, volumes and constraints: professional secrecy, data protection, tools already in place.

Steps.Title: Use case selection
Steps.Text: We rank the ideas by value, feasibility and risk, and we keep one or two. Cases where an error would cost too much, or where the rule cannot be written down, are set aside.

Steps.Title: Choice of model and hosting
Steps.Text: We test several models, proprietary and open source, on a sample of your documents, and we compare quality, cost and consequences for your data. You receive a reasoned recommendation, with its limits.

Steps.Title: Measured pilot
Steps.Text: The pilot runs on a limited scope, often alongside the existing process. The indicators are set before the start and measured on your own figures.

Steps.Title: Going into production
Steps.Text: Integration into your tools, access rights, logging, supervision, team training and a manual fallback procedure in case of an outage.

Steps.Title: Governance
Steps.Text: Who decides the rules, who changes them, who checks the errors, how often the model is reassessed. We document these points so that the system stays under control over time.

Technologies.Title: The technologies we work with
Technologies.Text: Proprietary models: OpenAI (including through Azure OpenAI), Anthropic, Mistral. Open-source models: Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, deployed on your infrastructure or in a Swiss cloud. Microsoft ecosystem: Microsoft 365, Copilot, Power Platform and Azure, when your teams already work there. We have no exclusivity with any vendor: the list changes as models change, and the choice is always made on your case.

ModelsHosting.Title: Models and hosting: how we choose
ModelsHosting.Intro: There is no best model in general. There is a model suited to a case, to certain data and to a budget. Here is how we reason.

Choice.Title: When to choose what
Choice.Text: A managed service from a major vendor suits varied, low-sensitivity tasks, small volumes and teams without operations skills. An open-source model hosted in Switzerland becomes interesting when the data is covered by professional or medical secrecy, when the task is repetitive and well defined, when volumes make pay-per-use billing expensive, or when you do not want to depend on a single supplier.

OpenSource.Title: Open-source models hosted in Switzerland
OpenSource.Text: Open models such as Llama, Mistral, Qwen or Gemma can be installed on your own servers or in a data centre in Switzerland. For targeted tasks such as sorting, extraction or summarising, they often give sufficient results, provided they are tested on your documents. Their licence varies from one model to another: we check it before any use.

Swiss.Title: What "hosted in Switzerland" means in practice
Swiss.Text: For each project we set four points in writing. Where inference runs: on machines located in Switzerland, either yours or those of a Swiss host. Where the data is: documents, indexes and results stay on that same infrastructure. Who has access: a named list of people, with limited rights. What is logged: decisions and accesses, without keeping more content than necessary. Hosting in Switzerland does not replace your own legal analysis; it simplifies it.

Proprietary.Title: Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic or Mistral, when it is the right choice
Proprietary.Text: If your teams live in Microsoft 365 and the content is already there, staying in that environment is often the simplest option. For complex drafting or reasoning tasks, the large proprietary models keep an edge. We then review with you the processing region, the contractual terms and data retention.

Limits.Title: What we do not promise
Limits.Text: A model sometimes makes mistakes. We do not sell certification, turnkey compliance or full automation. We design systems where the rules are yours, where doubtful cases go to a person and where every decision can be explained after the fact.

UseCases.Title: Typical scenarios
UseCases.Intro: Representative projects, described without a named client or quantified result.

Cases.Title: Minor liability claims in a medical institution
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. An open-source model hosted in Switzerland sorts a medical institution's minor liability claims: automatic settlement for files that meet the institution's rules, human review for all the others.

Cases.Title: Open source hosted in Switzerland or a US subscription
Cases.Summary: Decision guide. Data, cost, quality, maintenance, skills: the five criteria for choosing between an open-source model hosted in Switzerland and a US AI service, with a comparison table and the limits of each option.

Cases.Title: Small insurance claims
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. AI sorting separates the claims that can be settled directly from those that need a claims handler. The thresholds remain the insurer's and no refusal is automated.

Cases.Title: Invoices, expense reports and VAT at a fiduciary firm
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. Each document receives a proposed entry or a reasoned anomaly flag. The accountant validates conforming documents in batches and concentrates on the discrepancies.

Cases.Title: KYC files and AMLA alerts
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. The model checks that files are complete and ranks alerts by priority with a sourced summary. Closing alerts and any compliance decision remain human.

Cases.Title: Mail and email automation
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. An AI system classifies each incoming letter and email by type, extracts the key information, routes it to the right file and flags urgent items. Staff can then find any communication through semantic search, and a person validates the uncertain cases.

Cases.Title: Automatic deadline detection
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. A SharePoint application analyses documents to spot legal and contractual deadlines, then creates calendar events in Teams with progressive reminders. The detected deadlines remain to be confirmed by the person handling the file.

Cases.Title: Intelligent invoice payment reminders
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. Reminders for unpaid invoices are drafted by AI, with a tone and content adapted to how late the payment is and to the history of the relationship. Each message can be reviewed before it is sent.

Cases.Title: Automatic legal document summarization
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. A summarisation tool produces two levels of structured summary for reports and contracts, so that readers can quickly decide whether a full reading is needed. The summary does not replace reading the decisive passages.

Cases.Title: Contract drafting assistant
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. A Word add-in suggests clauses from a validated library, assembles a tailored draft contract and checks its consistency. Lawyers stay in control of the tailoring, the negotiation and the final approval.

Cases.Title: Predictive sales and inventory analysis
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. Predictive models analyse sales and stock history, enriched with contextual data, to anticipate seasonal peaks and prepare orders. The forecasts remain a decision aid and are compared with actual results.

Cases.Title: Knowledge base with semantic search
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. A knowledge base with semantic search understands the intent behind questions, and a model generates concise answers that cite their sources. It helps new team members in particular to find information.

Cases.Title: Meeting transcription and action extraction
Cases.Summary: Illustrative scenario. AI transcription of meetings produces a structured summary and creates a Planner task for each agreed action. A participant reviews the summary before it is shared.

Items.Title: Productivity gains
Items.Desc: Automate repetitive tasks and allow your teams to focus on high-value activities.

Items.Title: Cost reduction
Items.Desc: Lower your operational costs by optimizing your processes and reducing manual errors.

Items.Title: Better decision making
Items.Desc: Base your decisions on in-depth data analysis rather than intuition alone.

Items.Title: Competitive advantage
Items.Desc: Adopt the technologies that will make the difference against your competitors in the years to come.

TypicalSituations.Title: Typical situations
TypicalSituations.Disclaimer: Fictional, simplified examples of situations we can handle. They do not describe specific client projects or guaranteed results.

Cases.Situation: A claims or compliance team receives many files, most of which follow the same path, yet everything is read by hand.
Cases.WhatWeDo: Workshop to write your triage rules, a pilot with human validation on test files, then production with a decision log; model hosted in Switzerland where the data requires it.

Cases.Situation: An SME wants an assistant that answers from its procedures and contracts without those documents leaving Switzerland.
Cases.WhatWeDo: Cost comparison between a US subscription and an open-source model hosted in Switzerland, model choice, connection to the documents with the existing access rights, quality tests before opening it to the teams.

Cases.Situation: Management has received several “AI agency” proposals and cannot tell which are serious.
Cases.WhatWeDo: Review of the proposals, use cases ranked by value and risk, a step-by-step roadmap with stop criteria.
